name: ImpulseRC Apex 5" Freestyle Carbon Quad
notes: ImpulseRC has closed; its Apex mini-site (archived): "Motor to Motor 225mm - Fits 5.2\" Props", "Arms: 5.5mm, Key: 5mm, Lower Main: 2.5mm, Upper Main: 2mm, Top: 2mm", "Standoff Height Front: 28mm Rear: 20mm" (the front height is used), "Dry Weight Alu hardware: approx. 115g Steel hardware: approx. 125g" (115 g used), "Mounting positions are provided for M3 30x30 as well as M3 20x20". The archived product page (http://web.archive.org/web/20191120113744/https://impulserc.com/products/apex-5-frame-kit) lists the same plates and "(4x) M3 28mm Standoff". Motor mount pattern: TODO(source), not stated. frontalArea_m2 and dragCoefficient_cd: TODO(source), not published (the old 0.015 m² and 0.85 had no source), so there is no top-speed estimate. The earlier 138 g and 30.5 mm stack were not ImpulseRC's numbers.

name: Eclipson Model A 3D-Printable Plane (LW-PLA)
notes: Eclipson Model A page (the old /model-a URL is dead): LW-PLA / PLA columns "PRINTED WEIGHT 220g (LW-PLA) / 390g (PLA)", "TAKE OFF WEIGHT* 490g / 730g" (*including landing gear), "STALL SPEED 24km/h / 29 km/h", "WING LOADING 30g/dm² / 45g/dm²", "WING SPAN 1000mm", "WING SURFACE 16dm2", "WING ASPECT RATIO 6,6", "LENGTH 760mm", battery "2S or 3S, 500 mAh to 1500 mAh". The LW-PLA column is used: empty 220 g, stall 24 km/h = 6.67 m/s at its 490 g take-off weight (stallSpeed_at_490g_ms). Eclipson's standard power pack page (https://www.eclipson-airplanes.com/standardpowerpack): motor "MAX DIAMETER - 28mm", proposed Sunnysky X2212 1250 kV, propellers 8x6 (proposed), 7x6 or 8x5, 8x7. No maximum propeller is stated, so maxPropDiameter_in is null (TODO(source)). wingChord_mm 160 is DERIVED as mean chord = 16 dm² / 1.0 m. Airfoil, cl_max, cd0, rib count, spar diameter and motor mount: TODO(source), not published (the old NACA 2412, 1.25, 0.032, 14 ribs and 6 mm spar had no source; the old 1200 mm span, 820 mm length, 18.2 dm², 290 g and 650 g were not this airplane's numbers). With no cd0 the cruise power and endurance are not judged.

name: E-flite Convergence VTOL
notes: E-flite Convergence VTOL manual (EFL11050 BNF / EFL11075 PNP): "25.5 in (651mm)" wingspan, "26.9 in (682mm)" length, "291 in2 (1883 cm2)" wing area, weight "27.2 OZ (771.1 g)" (flyingWeight_g: the manual's flying weight, which includes a flight battery, so it is not an empty weight), "Motors: (2) 2210-1450Kv Main Motors, (1) 2730 - 1550Kv Tail Motor" (two tilting nacelles plus a fixed tail motor), "ESC: (3) 20 AMP", "Recommended Battery: 11.1V 3S 2200mAh 30C Li-Po", CG 154-168 mm, a 6-minute flight timer. Product page (https://www.horizonhobby.com/product/convergence-vtol-bnf-basic-650mm/EFL11050.html, discontinued): 650 mm span, 680 mm length, 2200-3000 mAh 3S. emptyWeight_g: TODO(source), not published, so a build on it is blocked until the airframe can be weighed. Propeller sizes (the manual gives part numbers EFL11003 / EFL11004 only), airfoil, tilt range, cl_max, cd0, stall and transition speeds: TODO(source), not published. The earlier record ("AeroHawk", 340 g empty, 850 g, 14.5 dm², MH 60 airfoil, 6-inch props, cl_max 1.15, cd0 0.042) was invented.

name: GEPRC CineLog25 V2 2.5" Cinewhoop
notes: Frame page: "Wheelbase:114mm", "Arm thickness: 2.5mm", top and bottom plate 2.0 mm, "FC dimension: 25.5mm x 25.5mm", "Motor dimension:: 9mm x 9mm", "Propellers: 2.5 inch propellers", "Weight: 70.9g±2". The page does not say what the 70.9 g includes; it is taken as the frame with its ducts. electronicsWeight_g is derived, not published: the Analog BNF (https://geprc.com/product/cinelog25-v2-analog-quadcopter/) weighs "148g±5g" with FC/ESC AIO, Caddx Ratel2 camera, 1 W VTX and receiver; 148 - 70.9 frame - 4 x 9.8 g GR1404 motors - 4 x 1.28 g HQ DT63x4 props = 32.8 g. Duct inner diameter and depth: TODO(source), not published by GEPRC. No published frontal area or drag coefficient, so no top-speed estimate. Published flight time on the BNF page: "4'00\" -6'00\"" on a 4S 660-850 mAh LiPo.

name: iFlight Chimera7 Pro V2 7" Long-Range
notes: O4 frame kit page: "Wheelbase: 327mm", "Arm Thickness: 6mm", "Bottom Plate Thickness: 3mm", "Top Plate Thickness: 2mm", "Flight Stack Mounting: 30*30", "Motor Mounting: 16x16mm / 19*19mm", "Weight: 355g±5g" (kit incl. TPU parts), L270 x W199 x H34 mm. No maximum propeller is stated; the page says it "pairs best with 2809 motors for optimal 7.5\" prop performance", so 7.5 in is used. electronicsWeight_g is derived, not published: the Chimera7 Pro V2 6S O4 HD BNF (https://shop.iflight.com/Chimera7-Pro-V2-6S-O4-HD-Pro2259) weighs "725±5g" without battery (BLITZ F722 FC, BLITZ E55 4-in-1 ESC, O4 air unit, GPS, receiver); 725 - 355 frame - 4 x 60.7 g XING2 2809 - 4 x 9.4 g HQ 7.5x3.7x3 props = 89.6 g. The same BNF page publishes "Takeoff Weight incl. 8000mAH: Approx. 1621±5g", "Max Speed: 140km/h" and "Max Hover Time: Approx. 30 min (No load With 21700 6S 8000mAH)". No frontal area or drag coefficient is published.

name: Tarot X6 960 mm Folding Hexacopter
notes: Tarot TL6X001. Retailer spec list: "Diagonal wheelbase: 960mm", "Net weight: 2.0kg", "Length of one arm: 392mm", "Weight of one arm: 113g", "Diameter of center plate: 328mm", "Max propeller size: 18 inches", "Ground clearance: 320mm (rail to ground)", "5 Degree Rotor Arm Dihedral", electric retractable landing gear, folding arms. Hex-X vs hex-+ orientation, arm tube diameter and motor-mount pattern: TODO(source), not published (the flight controller sets the orientation; the geometry is the same hexagon). electronicsWeight_g is derived, not published as one figure: 6 x T-Motor ALPHA 40A 6S ESC at "54.5g" each incl. cables (https://store.tmotor.com/goods.php?id=580) = 327 g, plus the dataset's 30 g flight-controller/wiring allowance (DRONE_RULES.ELECTRONICS_ALLOWANCE_G) = 357 g. GPS mast, power distribution and gimbal are not counted.

name: XUWING (Finwing) VTBIRD 1600 mm VTOL 4+1 QuadPlane
material: EPO foam, carbon spars and tubes, CNC aluminium VTOL mounts
notes: XUWING/Finwing VTBIRD 4+1 kit page (the 4+1 kit + power combo listing; the plain kit listing https://www.finwinghobby.com/goods.php?id=141 repeats the same specification block): "WingSpan: 1600MM", "Length: 1300MM", "WingArea: 40 SqDM", "Kit weight: 1.05kg (including VTOL 3K Arm but not including VTOL CNC parts)", "VTOL Frame 4+1 AUW: 4.5kg-5.5kg (Max. 5.5kg)", "Payload: 0.4kg-0.8kg", "Flight time: 1-2 hours", EPO airframe with carbon spars and CNC aluminium VTOL parts; the 4+1 uses a pusher, the kit includes "4+1 CNC parts and 3K Arms", landing gear is a 3D-printed set (file on the page) or a separate carbon gear, not included. The page's flight-test sheet (https://www.finwinghobby.com/images/upload/Image/VTBIRD%20VTOL%204+1%20Endurance%20flight%20testing%20data20201118.jpg) gives the built aircraft: two-battery mode "Battery totally 2.3kg, Plane AUW 5.3kg", one-battery mode "Weight 2.35kg, Plane AUW 5.35kg", "Cruising Speed: Airspeed 19m/s, Transition Speed 18m/S" (cruiseSpeed_ms, transitionSpeed_ms), 1 h 44-45 min and 95-122 km, on 4 x "X4112S 485KV" with "EOLO 1350" lift props and an "X3520 III 560KV" pusher on "EOLO 1480". The frame-types drawing (https://www.finwinghobby.com/images/upload/Image/VTBIRD-4%20Frame%20types2020_9_12.jpg) gives the 4+1 lift-motor diagonal as "720MM" (liftMotorDiagonal_mm) and "12\"-13\" Props" for lift, "13\"-14\" Props" for the pusher (so maxPropDiameter_in 13). emptyWeight_g 1050 is the published kit weight, which leaves the CNC VTOL mounts out. electronicsWeight_g is DERIVED, not published: Finwing's built test aircraft weighs 5.3 kg - 2.3 kg battery = 3.0 kg without battery; 3000 - 1050 kit - 4 x 169 g lift motors - 219 g pusher motor - 34 g pusher prop = 1021 g, which therefore holds the CNC VTOL mounts, the lift propellers (no published weight), servos, five ESCs, flight controller, GPS, wiring and landing gear, and any camera the test plane carried (Finwing does not say whether it carried one, so a fitted payload may be counted twice). The motor weights used are the Sunnysky records in this dataset (X4112S KV450 and X3520-III KV560), not Finwing's own 485KV lift motor, whose weight is not published. wingChord_mm 250 is DERIVED as mean chord = wing area / span = 0.40 m^2 / 1.6 m; aspect ratio (span^2 / area = 6.4) is left to the physics, which works it out the same way. Geometry from the product photos: twin round carbon tail booms from the fuselage to an H tail (a horizontal stabiliser with a fin at each end, no rudder), a pusher motor at the fuselage tail between the booms, and four separate carbon lift arms on pods under the wing, one motor ahead of the wing and one behind it on each side. Boom length and diameter, lift-arm length, the lift motors' spanwise and fore-aft spacing, the airfoil and the root chord: TODO(source), not published. cl_max and cd0: TODO(source), not published, so stall speed, cruise power, cruise endurance and range are not modelled; the published 19 m/s cruise speed is used for the speed check.
